label: SLAMJAM, phrases and the stage
notes: SLAMJAM, a second mode (GLO's list): a band and a robot poet make it up as they go. Thirteen ways to tell a poem, fourteen topics and eight bands, from jazz bar and boom bap to bossa, trap and punk. Your song is kept and comes back when you switch.

In SLAMJAM, HOME is Practice, where the band rehearses, and FX is the SLAMJAM room, where the poet performs. The four knobs are the four players' styles; turn one to "yours" and that part is yours to play and record.
In the room the Voice's black keys give the poet a tune: play as many notes as the next line has syllables and he sings it to them.

Songs are written a phrase at a time and arranged into a song: SEQ shows the phrase, HOME + SEQ the song. Voice, Keys and Bass are written at a cursor: tap a key to write a note, hold it and turn SELECT to stretch it.
Every syllable needs a note: a phrase can't be left, nor the song saved, until its words and notes match, and the screen says how many are missing.
Hold any button alone for a help card: what the screen is and what every button and knob does there.
What you change is heard as you change it: a sound picked, a knob turned, a note the cursor lands on, the key's chord when ROOT or SCALE turns.
SCALE in GLO keeps every key you play in key, and the arpeggiator (ARP) plays Keys and Bass up and down their chords.
Mister Wiggles has a stage: the karaoke room, Sing and the Voice's pages put him in front of a wall of lit screens, and what you change shows on it.
Loading a song or switching modes while one plays stops it first; imported songs find their key; a few words that broke the voice are said properly now.

label: Lyrics on two lines
notes: A long lyric line breaks in two at a word edge, with the robot a little higher, so the whole line shows.
A rest of two bars or more shows a bar filling where the words go, like a karaoke video; for its last two half notes the next line's words come back.

label: Song import and sync
notes: Better song importing.
Sync saves songs to their slots reliably.

label: Public Release Candidate
notes: Sings: import a karaoke (.kar) or MIDI song, or type a line on the FM-1 and play its notes on the keys; the voice is the 386 DX Engine, sung to your pitches and lengths.
Typing a line: the FM-1 counts its syllables, then you play a key for each one. Lines can be reordered, moved, and copied by reference, so a chorus is written once.
The face is the voice: it hops with the pitch, wobbles with vibrato, opens its mouth with the sound, and wears ^ ^ eyes on high notes and – – eyes on low ones.
Four tracks: Voice, Keys, Bass and Drums, with sound lists, a step sequencer (hold a step to edit it), live recording, tempo, and Voice settings you can change mid-song.
Sixteen punch-in effects under your fingers, several at once. The key lights show where you are (every fourth key) and blink the last one used.
Eight song slots with LOAD, SAVE TO, NEW SONG and RENAME SONG. Greensleeves is in S1 the first time it starts, and you can write over it.
This page installs and updates 386DX itself, puts songs into the slots, downloads or deletes them (queue the changes, then Sync), and runs the firmware in the browser.
Thirteen public-domain standards come with the page, ready to put in a slot.
